frontier-citation-graph.charter.{question,hypothesis,why_now,non_duplication}: the premise 'the citation graph is only a 250-decision sample' is false as stated. Accepted artifacts already contain a corpus-scale graph: evaluation/evaluation/build_174k_citation_graph.py, evaluation/evaluation/results/174k_citation_heritage/citation_graph_174k.json (5,031 source decisions, 7,799 edges, 1,286 nodes with outdegree>=2) and citation_pairs_174k_full.json (137,314 positive pairs). Acknowledge these artifacts, state why they were not adopted into the frozen benchmark (e.g. bge_/bger_ ID mismatch or the shared>=2 criterion), and reframe the team as extending/validating/integrating them rather than rebuilding from the 250-node seed; update non_duplication accordingly so the team does not redo existing corpus-scale extraction.

frontier-citation-graph.charter.acceptance_test item (1): the primary target '>=100k decisions carrying at least one resolved outgoing edge' exceeds the corpus citation-field ceiling. The charter's own dependency cites cited_decisions field coverage = 0.526 (validation_report_v14.json, sample_size 1000; count 526), so at most ~91,584 of 174,113 decisions can carry any outgoing citation, and the existing scaled graph resolves only 5,031 source decisions. Replace with a target bounded by the field ceiling (e.g. '>=90% of decisions whose cited_decisions field is non-empty') and keep the documented-ceiling fallback explicit.

The redirection is mission-aligned and does break the no-material-change supervisor loop, but it is not yet correct enough to integrate.
